newsitem.title: UK: British insurers asked for views on gene testing.
newsitem.headline: British insurers asked for views on gene testing.

text.p: Britain's Human Genetics Advisory Commission (HGAC) said on Wednesday it would ask insurance companies what they thought about genetic testing.

"The aim of the two-month consultation is to invite a broad range of opinion within the industry and beyond on issues such as how genetic tests are interpreted by insurers and how decisions are made, the extent of the information collected and questions of confidentiality and security," it said in a statement.
Advances in technology mean that tests are available, or soon will be, for genetic susceptibility to illnesses such as cancer or Alzheimer's disease.
Testing is already common for Huntington's disease, a rare genetic disorder that causes dementia and death.
There have been fears that insurance companies could require clients to submit to tests and could raise premiums for those found to have genes predisposing to illness.
